subject: Brightlane POC — orchestration handoff & evaluation checkpoints
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Lexi Park <lexi@brightlane.ai>, Anil Shah <anil@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Brightlane POC — orchestration handoff & evaluation checkpoints

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on goals. Summarizing the proposed POC scope and immediate handoff items so we have a shared checklist to move faster. I attached a short POC checklist and preliminary SDK samples.

High-level objective:
- Prove Redwood reduces inference cost while meeting Brightlane latency SLO for inference-heavy workflows (transactional enrichment pipeline).

Success criteria (proposed):
- End-to-end inference latency p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms on Brightlane dev data (100k token/day simulation)
- Per-token cost delta <= 40% vs current baseline (measured by unit tests we share)
- Functional parity on output quality for the enrichment model (BLEU/ROUGE/TBD evaluation set)
- Stable streaming behavior for the live enrichment path (no dropped events over 1 hour continuous load test)

Scope / Deliverables:
- Integration using Redwood SDK + API routes for both streaming and batch evaluation
- Instrumentation: token-level cost and trace headers enabled for comparison runs
- One-week performance run followed by a 72-hour soak test

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (next 3 business days): tech kickoff + credentials exchange + brief architecture review
- Week 1: SDK integration and first smoke tests (sample 10k messages)
- Week 2: Performance tuning and quality evals
- Week 3: Soak test and final acceptance rubric evaluation

Ownership ask:
- Brightlane: provide sample dataset (redacted) + engineering point-of-contact for SDK integration (API keys will be short-lived for the POC)
- Redwood: integration lead (Marissa) + runtime engineer (Jasmine) for tech syncs and telemetry setup

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Please confirm the Brightlane engineering lead for the POC and a preferred time for the tech kickoff (30–45 min).
2) Share a sanitized sample of the enrichment payloads (up to 10k rows) and the expected quality checks.
3) Confirm any specific security requirements (IP allowlist, SFTP for sample, required SOC artifacts).

Attachments:
- redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx (POC milestones + acceptance template)
- prelim-sdk-samples.zip (example calls: generate, stream, embeddings)

Thanks — I’ll schedule the tech kickoff once I have your preferred time slots.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Lexi Park <lexi@brightlane.ai>

Subject: Re: Brightlane POC — orchestration handoff & evaluation checkpoints

Thanks Jasmine — this is helpful. A couple clarifying Qs before the kickoff: 

- SDK compatibility: Our stack is Node (server-side) + a Go data pipeline. Are the SDK samples in the zip runnable for both runtimes or will we need language bindings?
- Streaming semantics: for our enrichment path we need server-sent events with incremental structured chunks (JSONL) and a strict ordering guarantee. Can Redwood guarantee ordering when requests are sharded across multiple workers?
- Tool-calling: we discussed a potential tool flow where the model suggests an internal lookup call (account lookup). Can you outline how function/tool calling is handled and whether we can route those calls through our own service?

We’ll aim to get a redacted dataset to you by Monday if that timeline works. Our engineering lead for POC will be me and I’ll assign Anil as the implementation owner; I’m cc’ing procurement (procurement@brightlane.ai) so they can prep any paperwork.

Lexi
VP Product, Brightlane
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Lexi Park <lexi@brightlane.ai>, Anil Shah <anil@brightlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Mar 2028 19:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightlane POC — orchestration handoff & evaluation checkpoints

Lexi — great questions. Answering in order and adding practical notes for the tech kickoff.

1) SDK compatibility
- The attached prelim-sdk-samples.zip contains: nodejs/ and go/ example folders. Both include a small client wrapper and sample calls. If you prefer language bindings, we can drop a dedicated Go module and a scoped NPM package for the POC.

2) Streaming semantics and ordering
- Redwood supports chunked streaming via SSE and HTTP/2 chunked responses. For ordered delivery, the runtime pins a request to a single worker for the duration of the stream when the request includes a persistent session header (x-rw-session-id). That ensures ordering across chunks. For high throughput we recommend session affinity at the client side or a short-lived sticky token we provide for the POC.

3) Tool/function calling and routing
- Redwood supports the function-calling spec (JSON schema for inputs/outputs). Calls from the model to external tools are surfaced to the client as structured events. You can:
  a) Receive the call on the client side and execute it within Brightlane infra (recommended for PII-sensitive lookups).
  b) Route the call through a Redwood-managed adapter if you prefer us to mediate (useful for complex rate limiting).
- Security note: function outputs can be redacted at the adapter layer; for PII we suggest performing lookups inside Brightlane and returning only non-sensitive keys.

Integration specifics (POC):
- API routes:
  - POST /v1/generate — synchronous generation endpoint (supports max tokens and stop sequences)
  - POST /v1/stream — streaming endpoint (SSE). include x-rw-session-id for ordering guarantees.
  - POST /v1/embeddings — batch and single-item endpoints for embedding scoring
- Auth: Bearer token for POC. For Dedicated or Private we support IP allowlists and customer-managed KMS.
- Telemetry: include x-rw-trace-id and x-rw-client-version headers to correlate traces in the Redwood Console. We’ll provide a small shim that injects those headers automatically in the Node/Go wrappers.
- Caching: we recommend prefix caching for repeated prompts and KV cache for partial prompt reuse; we’ll share a config suggestion based on your token distribution after we see the sample payload.

Attached: integration-snippets.md (short code samples and curling examples).

Suggested near-term plan before kickoff:
- You: share sanitized payload + one example enrichment lookup flow (JSON)
- Us: provision POC keys and a sticky-session token, prepare Node/Go wrappers and a short runbook for the tech sync
- Tech kickoff: 30–45 minutes (we can do 9–10:30am PT on Monday or Tuesday)

I’ll put together a brief runbook and push the Drive link to the thread.

Best,
Jasmine
